items.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: I have a piano player in San Diego, Pamela York, who is really great, and she and I get together every week and beat up on each other.

ctx.x: How do you go about learning all the tunes required to get you through a weekend like this?

There is no cramming for this exam. You cannot do that. Actually a year ago it was one of those situations where I realized I was really lacking. I would be able to sing tunes, but to remember the changes and stuff, I was just kicking my rear end. So I made a goal that I was going to learn five tunes a week. And so just pick an album, pick a CD and you just start going through it. And then I have a piano player in San Diego, Pamela York, who is © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

really great, and she and I get together every week and beat up on each other. Okay I’m going to learn these songs, well I’m going to learn these. Okay. So then we challenge each other and we’ll say “Stella By Starlight” up a major third every chorus. But you know Ray Brown told me, I had a lesson with him, and I did this song, he wrote this tune “Benny,” and I did a lyric to it. And I was ready for this lesson with him a year ago. I went in and I’m just like I’m going to just swing the snot out of this thing.…
